classes.schedule: Wednesdays 7pm-10pm PT · Nov 11 - Jan 23 · 8 sessions + class show
classes.level: Improv 201: The Game of the Scene
classes.description:
Building upon the concepts of Improv 101, students will begin discovering UCB’s philosophy of Game! Students learn to recognize patterns and comedic themes within scenes and how to heighten these elements for maximum comedic impact. Students will also be introduced to new concepts such as editing, second beats, and more. Take the next step in your improv journey with 201!

Course meets for 8 sessions, each 3 hours long. There is one class performance after the final session.
classes.location: Franklin Campus: Annex, 1925 N Bronson Ave, Los Angeles

classes.title: Improv Level One
classes.description: From day one you will jump into a series of fun warm ups and games designed to ease you into improv. Before you know it you will be playing scenes and learning how to heighten and explore your ideas. As the class progresses you will learn how to do 2 person scenes, group scenes, group games and how to deliver simple monologues. The class is all about fun and support. Whether you are a beginner who has never improvised or someone who has improv experience, you will learn strong fundamentals that will build your confidence, improve speaking skills and foster spontaneity

classes.title: Advanced Study Improv: Forms! Forms! Forms!
classes.schedule: Thursdays 7pm-10pm ET · Nov 12 - Dec 19 · 5 sessions + class show
classes.description: Wanna hear something wild? The Harold is not the only improv show format! I know. You've heard people say, "Spokane. Slacker. Monoscene. LeRonde. Close Quarters." But what do they mean? In this class, you will be introduced to a new improv form each week and increase your vocabulary on different styles and devices.
classes.location: Union Square, 113 University Place, Sixth Floor, New York

classes.title: Drop-In: Intro to BCC Improv w/ Andy Junk (Thursday, November 12th, 2026)
classes.description:
This Intro class teaches you what the BCC’s approach to improv is all about - how to say both FUCK IT and LOVE IT while performing. FUCK IT means you don’t worry about the outcome or result of your efforts. You are not judging whether you perform things correctly or whether you make mistakes. You are simply committed to doing what you are doing without worrying whether it is good or not. LOVE IT means you celebrate the whimsy, joy, and delight inherent in making shit up onstage. You remember why you fell in love with improv, one of the most wonderful feelings in the world. Learn to hold both of these ideas in your head at the same time and create fearless, fun, and dumb improv.

If you are new to improv, this workshop will set you up for a fearless way to begin learning. If you are an experienced improviser, this workshop will introduce you to a new philosophy of improv that is different than other improv schools in NYC. Either way you will be challenged and motivated!

This class is designed for students new to BCC’s approach to improv.

Drop-in Class: Thursday, November 12th, 7:00PM - 9:30PM

Where: BCC DogHouse, Studio #2 (137 Montrose Ave, Brooklyn)

Each class is limited to 16 students.

classes.title: Lyric Writing for Comedy
classes.description:
Lyric Writing for Comedy is for anyone who is excited to learn or refine their skills in comedic songwriting. This one day class will help you understand the different structures to use when writing your comedy song. We’ll look at examples of songs (both funny and not!) that will help you think about the best way to get your comedic topic across. We will learn how to use structure in a way that feels the most freeing for you!

Come in with an idea of what you want to write about for class. No need to create music but a plus if you already have a melody you want to work on! We will read or sing the song you decide to make!
classes.location: Union Square, 113 University Place, Sixth Floor, New York

classes.title: How to Write a Short Humor Piece with Caitlin Kunkel
classes.description:
Do you want to write funny in 750 words or less? Do you have something to say on a topic you know well? Do you crave fun, need an outlet for your creativity, and hunger for more bylines? Then, short humor is for you.

In this two-hour class, writer and comedy craft book author Caitlin Kunkel will teach a repeatable process for writing a short humor piece in the style of McSweeney’s Internet Tendency, The Belladonna, Points in Case, and other online sites (note: we will not cover satirical news like The Onion or Reductress).

You’ll learn how to brainstorm, find a structure for your piece, craft a strong comedic premise and title, and use the two-list system of joke writing to fast draft a humor piece. Come ready to write and leave with a new piece and a set process to write even more in the future.

All participants will receive a copy of Inside Jokes: A Comedy and Creativity Guide For All Writers.
classes.location: Second City Training Center, Chicago

classes.title: Musical Improv 201
classes.schedule: Fridays 2:30pm-5:30pm PT · Nov 13 - Jan 23 · 8 sessions + class show
classes.description:
Now that you know *how* to improvise a song, it's time to learn *what* to sing! 201 explores song types typically used in musicals, finding the game in your songs, and getting even more comfortable with being on stage singing!

Students will continue to work with an accompanist using song structures, and then by creating their own structures as they go along. By learning to work with and create their own rhythms and patterns, students will gain skills that they can apply to all forms of Improv.

classes.title: Acting for Sketch
classes.description:
In this class we’ll work on approaches to acting in short comedy sketches. We’ll focus on things like strong character choices, understanding the beats of a sketch, emotional heightening and commitment.
The sketch performer is essential to finding and building the game of the sketch. A well-rounded sketch performer has character range as well as the ability to ground the scene through believable acting choices and we’ll endeavor to give you the tools to get there!

classes.title: Workshop: You Already Did The Funny Thing with Jeff Quintana
classes.description:
Improvisers spend so much time searching for the games that they often miss all the funny shit they've already created. In this workshop, we'll explore how the first 30 seconds of a scene can reveal multiple games through your own comedic behaviors, your connection to your scene partner, and your connection to the audience. Through specific exercises and scene work, you'll learn to recognize these patterns, discover different levels of game, and build on what's already happening instead of constantly searching for something new.

classes.title: Improv + Scene Work for TV & Film with Casting Director SJ Allocco-St. Germain
classes.description:
Casting Director & Producer SJ Allocco-St. Germain will take actors through the fundamentals of performing for television and film, with a focus on naturalism, comedy, improvisation, and making strong choices on camera.

SJ will teach you how to:

· adjust your performance for the camera
· make bold choices without overplaying
· use improv to enhance scripted scenes
· listen and genuinely react on camera
· find the comedy without forcing it
· make strong, specific character choices
· take direction and make quick adjustments
· approach TV/film auditions with confidence
· understand what casting directors are looking for
· make your self-tape stand out

The workshop will include scene work, mock auditions, and individual coaching, giving actors the opportunity to put the techniques into practice and receive direct feedback from SJ.
classes.location: 14th Street Campus, 239 E 14th Street, New York City

classes.title: ONLINE Pilot Writing
classes.description:
In this course, you will take an idea from a pitch all the way to a polished draft of your very own half hour comedy pilot, getting feedback at each step as you go through this tough but really rewarding process. We'll talk about elements of a strong comedy pilot concept, character creation, outline structure, and how to write dialogue that sounds like it comes from a human. And we'll do it in a supportive workshop environment where you'll be giving feedback on other projects as you work on your own.

This class will break down the comedy pilot writing process into easily achieved weekly goals. You will leave with a completed draft that you can build on and use as a sample. If writing a pilot feels overwhelming, this is the class for you.
classes.location: Online

classes.description: In this workshop we'll discuss generating ideas from a blank page. We'll learn tips and tricks to spark our creativity and discuss useful tools to hone our skills as conscious comedic observers. In addition, we'll take these kernels of ideas or interesting observations and mine them.

classes.schedule: Mondays 7pm-10pm ET · Nov 16 - Jan 16 · 8 sessions + class show
classes.description:
Building upon the skills learned in Improv 101 & 201, Improv 301 is where students begin to dive into The Harold, learning the structure as well as how to generate ideas from new openings! Students will develop a deeper understanding of scene dynamics and work together to build group games. By the end of this course, students will be comfortable with pulling ideas from an opening, finding and playing game in scenes, committing to character choices, in addition to working as an ensemble to build upon the structure of the Harold.

This course meets for 8 sessions, 3 hours each and culminates with a show at UCB.
classes.location: 14th Street Campus, 239 E 14th Street, New York City

classes.title: Public Speaking
classes.description: Do you want to become a better public speaker? Do you feel nervous, unsure or even dread when you give presentations and speeches? This class will give you the tools and skills necessary to deliver effective and engaging speeches. You will learn and practice public speaking theory in a way that is fun and challenging. This class provides participants with a theoretical foundation of public speaking along with several opportunities to practice, refine and reinforce their learning. Develop greater public speaking success professionally and personally.
classes.location: Second City Training Center, 230 W. North Ave, Chicago

classes.title: Improv 101
classes.schedule: Tuesdays 11am-2pm PT · Nov 17 - Jan 17 · 8 sessions + class show
classes.description: In Improv 101, students will be introduced to the fundamentals of improvisation through games, group exercises and scene work - all guaranteed to be fun and engaging. You will learn the core tenets of long form improv with a focus on agreement, active listening, portraying characters and playing to the top of your intelligence. These concepts act as building blocks for our subsequent classes as students learn to develop their own unique comedic voice. Whether you are looking to become a performer or step out of your comfort zone, this is the place to start!

classes.location: UCB Silver Lake, 2829 Sunset Blvd, Los Angeles

classes.title: Drop-In: Intro to Clown w/ Emma Simon (Tuesday, November 17th, 2026)
classes.description:
“It's you, of course, the clown. And that's important." -Nader Farman

What happens in a clown class? We introduce ourselves, we have a nice long warmup, our feet get squishy and our heads get floaty, we play with tennis balls and hats, we do group games and solo exercise from some of the greats (Lecoq, Conway, Johnstone) while working on taming their ego and bringing out their true inner clown. Come to just one class, come to all of them, do what your heart desires. You’ll probably leave with a new friend.

We're in an era of cognitive dissonance, hence all this clown talk. Absurd times call for an absurd response. Clown is antifascist and you are brave!

Class: Tuesday, November 17th, 7:00 PM - 9:30 PM

Where: BCC Pig Pen, Studio B (130 Graham Ave)

Each class is limited to 14 students.

classes.title: Headshot Dayz
classes.description:
Need a new headshot or refresh?

Look no further…

Chicago-based photographer, Timothy Schmidt, brings more than a decade of experience shooting headshots and portraits for working actors, celebrities and various red carpet an music events. You’ve likely seen his work around The Second City, showcasing all of the stages and casts over the last decade, including mainstage, ETC., Toronto and New York.

The Second City is now offering exclusive headshot sessions to currently enrolled students, where you will receive an “insiders” discount. This special price includes 3 professionally retouched studio headshot options and will be sent to you via a download link.

To take advantage of this special rate, you will need to come dressed in your first-choice outfit and bring a second wardrobe option (i.e. Shirts, jackets, accessories, are best for a quick change).

Please arrive camera ready with hair and makeup done. (Studio lights accentuate any oil on the skin so light foundation or powder is highly recommended for all.) Best practices are to show up 15 minutes early to give yourself a buffer and finalize your “last looks”. The more prepared you arrive, the better your shots will be! The photoshoot will be in studio on a white, gray, blue, or yellow backdrop.

If you are interested in taking advantage of this offer, visit @timothymschmidt on Instagram or www.TimothyMSchmidt.com for examples of Tim’s work and to find out options for dates and times.

classes.title: ONLINE Pilot Writing
classes.description:
In this course, you will take an idea from a pitch all the way to a polished draft of your very own half hour comedy pilot, getting feedback at each step as you go through this tough but really rewarding process. We'll talk about elements of a strong comedy pilot concept, character creation, outline structure, and how to write dialogue that sounds like it comes from a human. And we'll do it in a supportive workshop environment where you'll be giving feedback on other projects as you work on your own.

This class will break down the comedy pilot writing process into easily achieved weekly goals. You will leave with a completed draft that you can build on and use as a sample. If writing a pilot feels overwhelming, this is the class for you.

classes.title: Intro to Improv
classes.description: Looking to start your improv journey but not ready to commit to a full term of classes? Intro to Improv offers a fun and low pressure way to dive into the basics of improvisation. In this 4-week course, you’ll explore essential skills like saying “Yes, And,” making offers, and active listening. You’ll also start building trust with your ensemble and discover the joy of spontaneity and creative risk-taking. This class is designed to give you a solid foundation while fitting into your schedule.

classes.title: Drop-In: Intro to BCC Improv w/ Andy Junk (Thursday, November 19th, 2026)
classes.description:
This Intro class teaches you what the BCC’s approach to improv is all about - how to say both FUCK IT and LOVE IT while performing. FUCK IT means you don’t worry about the outcome or result of your efforts. You are not judging whether you perform things correctly or whether you make mistakes. You are simply committed to doing what you are doing without worrying whether it is good or not. LOVE IT means you celebrate the whimsy, joy, and delight inherent in making shit up onstage. You remember why you fell in love with improv, one of the most wonderful feelings in the world. Learn to hold both of these ideas in your head at the same time and create fearless, fun, and dumb improv.

If you are new to improv, this workshop will set you up for a fearless way to begin learning. If you are an experienced improviser, this workshop will introduce you to a new philosophy of improv that is different than other improv schools in NYC. Either way you will be challenged and motivated!

This class is designed for students new to BCC’s approach to improv.

Drop-in Class: Thursday, November 19th, 7:00PM - 9:30PM

Where: BCC DogHouse, Studio #2 (137 Montrose Ave, Brooklyn)

Each class is limited to 16 students.

Look no further…

Chicago-based photographer, Timothy Schmidt, brings more than a decade of experience shooting headshots and portraits for working actors, celebrities and various red carpet an music events. You’ve likely seen his work around The Second City, showcasing all of the stages and casts over the last decade, including mainstage, ETC., Toronto and New York.

The Second City is now offering exclusive headshot sessions to currently enrolled students, where you will receive an “insiders” discount. This special price includes 3 professionally retouched studio headshot options and will be sent to you via a download link.

To take advantage of this special rate, you will need to come dressed in your first-choice outfit and bring a second wardrobe option (i.e. Shirts, jackets, accessories, are best for a quick change).

Please arrive camera ready with hair and makeup done. (Studio lights accentuate any oil on the skin so light foundation or powder is highly recommended for all.) Best practices are to show up 15 minutes early to give yourself a buffer and finalize your “last looks”. The more prepared you arrive, the better your shots will be! The photoshoot will be in studio on a white, gray, blue, or yellow backdrop.

If you are interested in taking advantage of this offer, visit @timothymschmidt on Instagram or www.TimothyMSchmidt.com for examples of Tim’s work and to find out options for dates and times.

classes.schedule: Fridays 3pm-6pm PT · Nov 20 - Jan 31 · 8 sessions + class show
classes.description:
Building upon the skills learned in Improv 101 & 201, Improv 301 is where students begin to dive into The Harold, learning the structure as well as how to generate ideas from new openings! Students will develop a deeper understanding of scene dynamics and work together to build group games. By the end of this course, students will be comfortable with pulling ideas from an opening, finding and playing game in scenes, committing to character choices, in addition to working as an ensemble to build upon the structure of the Harold.

This course meets for 8 sessions, 3 hours each and culminates with a show at UCB.

classes.title: LGBTQIA+ Community Improv Jam
classes.description:
LGBTQIA+ Community Improv Jams

The Second City Training Center’s goal is to provide a safe environment for LGBTQ+ students across the larger improv community to come together and play freely. This event is free; no experience is required and participants do not have to be enrolled in a Second City class to participate. We do ask that those planning to attend register in advance for the event.

The LGBTQIA+ Jam is for people who identify as Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer, Intersex, and Asexual and all of the other identities not encompassed in the short acronym only and the jam will be hosted by a LGBTQIA+ faculty member.

classes.schedule: Saturdays 11am-2pm ET · Nov 21 - Jan 31 · 8 sessions + class show
classes.description: In Improv 101, students will be introduced to the fundamentals of improvisation through games, group exercises and scene work - all guaranteed to be fun and engaging. You will learn the core tenets of long form improv with a focus on agreement, active listening, portraying characters and playing to the top of your intelligence. These concepts act as building blocks for our subsequent classes as students learn to develop their own unique comedic voice. Whether you are looking to become a performer or step out of your comfort zone, this is the place to start!

classes.title: Physical Comedy Intensive: John Towsen (Saturday, November 21st, 2026)
classes.description:
In this one-day introduction to physical comedy you will be exposed to a few elements of physical comedy vocabulary involving everyday objects, learning new skills that you probably didn't even know existed. With every skill we explore, we will immediately be searching for comedy applications involving character and situation as a stepping stone to creating material. From there we will go on to exploring gag structures such as the escalating gag, the visual gag, the 3-part gag, and the oblivious gag, Participants will get to work on short pieces together since the whole point of the workshop is the integration of technique with story and character. No particular skill level, body type, or background is needed to be in the workshop, which I hope will be useful and FUN for everyone.

Intensive: Saturday, November 21st, 11:30 AM - 6:30 PM (with lunch break).

Where: BCC Mouse Trap (168A Johnson Ave, Brooklyn)

Each class is limited to 14 students.
classes.location: BCC Mouse Trap, 168A Johnson Ave, Brooklyn

classes.title: World Building And Connections with Frank Caeti
classes.description:
You have just performed the first couple of scenes of your long form, now what? This class will focus on using scenes you have performed earlier in any long form structure to inspire new scenes, build the world, and make strong connections. Students will learn techniques like time-dash, analogous situation, theme, pattern recognition, character, location, and following the fun – are all worthwhile threads to pursue for the second beat and beyond.

Prerequisite: Some improv experience helpful but not necessary.
classes.location: Second City Training Center, Chicago

classes.title: Improv Drop-In
classes.description: Thinking about trying improv? Our in-person drop-in classes are the perfect non-committal taste. No prior experience is necessary for these fun, relaxed introductions to some of the skills of improvised comedy. Meet new people, learn games & exercises and share 90-minutes of laughs each time you join us.

classes.title: Sketch Director Lab
classes.description:
A one-day intensive for comedians, improvisers, and sketch performers looking to bring their ideas to life on camera. Through hands-on exercises and a collaborative production day, students will learn the fundamentals of directing comedy—including working with actors, visual storytelling, and directing for performance.

By the end of the workshop, every student will have directed, edited, and screened their own short comedy scene while receiving feedback from the group. Ideal for students with prior Improv 101 or Sketch 101 experience (or equivalent) who are ready to step behind the camera.

Please note: There will be a 30 minute break during this class.
classes.location: UCB Silver Lake, 2829 Sunset Blvd, Los Angeles

classes.title: Sketch 201
classes.description:
This class will help you foster your individual voice as a writer as you are held to weekly writing deadlines. This class will offer you opportunities to pitch ideas to others and collaborate with other students on assignments in class. You will also get to hone individual pieces through rewriting.

Students must bring 4-6 sketch pitches to the FIRST session. Students should be prepared to devote time outside of class to completing new writing assignments for every session

The class will end with each student receiving individual feedback from the instructor on their own sketch packet.
classes.location: Franklin Campus: Upstairs, 5927 Franklin Ave - 2nd Floor, Los Angeles

classes.title: Drop-In: Improvised Sketch w/ Disco Horses (Sunday, November 22nd, 2026)
classes.description:
In this class you will learn how to take the basic fundamentals of improv and work with it to generate scenes, sketches, and characters that you can take and continue to shape. Starting with the core principles of good improv; yes, and, comedic game, and world-building (who, what, where), and combining that with a basic formula for sketch writing, you will be able to start from any base or premise and lead to a functioning scene on the spot.

The course will focus on the two main points of entry of improv-to-sketch that Joe and Eric have found great success in, answering questions and understanding formula. Learning how to spot moments that will lead to better improvised scenes that lead to sketch is a skill that will come from this workshop. The class will be split into two portions. The first of which Joe and Eric will dive into their points of improv-to-sketch, and the second will be active, asking participants to practice the skills and points discussed earlier in the class.

It is recommended that you have a bit of sketch and/or improv experience (classes, performances, writing alone in your basement) before you take this workshop, however it is not required.

If you are interested in learning how to create sketches from improv efficiently and consistently, then this workshop is for you!

Workshop: Sunday, November 22nd, 3:00pm-5:30pm

Where: BCC Pig Pen Theater (144 Boerum Street)

Workshop limited to 14 students.
classes.location: BCC Pig Pen Theater, 144 Boerum Street, Brooklyn

classes.title: Sketch 101
classes.description:
This course is an introduction to the UCB philosophy on sketch comedy, specifically using "the game" to write short comedic scenes. Each week students will engage in writing exercises that will explore different sketch formats. Students will be exposed to different methods for turning funny ideas into even funnier written sketches. Students will leave the class with an understanding of popular sketch formats and a portfolio of writing.

No prior sketch writing experience is necessary -- the only requirement for this class is a desire to write and learn. Students should have access to a computer, preparing sketches for presentation in every class. If you don't have access to a suitable tablet or computer, email johnny@ucbcomedy.com for possible solution
classes.location: Franklin Campus: Upstairs, 5927 Franklin Ave - 2nd Floor, Los Angeles

classes.title: Slow Comedy (4 sessions, in-person)
classes.description: In the beginning there was only slow comedy. And it was really funny. And G-d said it was good. In this class you will learn how to improvise longer, deeper, more finely detailed scenes. We believe that if you can do slow comedy, then you can play fast, but not necessarily the other way around. You will learn techniques that lead to improvised scenes that organically build to a place where the comedy is based on something more than a simple joke. Students will learn how to do more with less, make important discoveries, listen and react to subtext, and surprise each other and themselves. Prerequisite: Magnet Improv Level Two
classes.location: Michael Howard Studios - Studio 2, 152 W. 25th Street, 10th fl, New York

classes.level: Improv 201: The Game of the Scene
classes.description:
Building upon the concepts of Improv 101, students will begin discovering UCB’s philosophy of Game! Students learn to recognize patterns and comedic themes within scenes and how to heighten these elements for maximum comedic impact. Students will also be introduced to new concepts such as editing, second beats, and more. Take the next step in your improv journey with 201!

Course meets for 8 sessions, each 3 hours long. There is one class performance after the final session.

classes.title: Sketch 301
classes.schedule: Sundays 3:30pm-6:30pm ET · Nov 29 - Jan 30 · 8 sessions + class show
classes.description:
Students in this class will work together to write an original sketch show. Students will be held to weekly deadlines in order to generate material to be featured in the show. Students will also get the experience of generating material collaboratively with others.

Students will be expected to devote time to writing and rewriting material outside of class. Students will also get the experience of rehearsing, blocking, and producing sketches for the stage.

The culmination of Sketch 301 will be the performance of a sketch show comprised of student-generated material.

PLEASE NOTE: Students will be writing for a predetermined cast, not for themselves. The focus of the class is on writing, rewriting and producing sketches for the stage.

Sketch 301 also includes a mandatory Tech Rehearsal before the final performance. Students must be available to attend the Tech Rehearsal

in order to participate in the show and pass the course. Please check to make sure that you are available for the tech rehearsal before signing up for the course.

Students must bring a sketch to the FIRST session of class. This sketch should be written for the stage and no longer than four pages. This first sketch should be written utilizing the concept of the "Game of the Scene," taught in Sketch 101 and Sketch 201. Students should be prepared to devote time outside of class to completing new writing assignments for every session.

Course meets for 8 sessions, each 3 hours long. There is a class performance after the final session and a mandatory tech rehearsal.
classes.location: 14th Street Campus, 239 E 14th Street, New York City

classes.title: Advanced Improv L2
classes.description:
Advanced Improv 2 picks up right where Advanced Level 1 leaves off and bridges the gap between such forms as The Piñata and The Harold. The class culminates in a four week run of shows.

Prerequisite: Advanced Improv Level 1

classes.title: Advanced Special Effects
classes.description: Without props, sets or costumes the improviser has the freedom to manipulate an audience's perception of space and time to a degree limited only by his or her imagination. In this 8-week class students will explore the great potential of the empty space. The class will play with transformations, split scenes, swinging doors, journey scenes, morphs, novelty edits and more to expand and heighten scene work and piece dynamics. Prerequisite: Adv Improv Level One (or Magnet Improv Level 5).

classes.title: Musical Improv Level Two
classes.description:
Taking the fundamentals you learned in level one, Musical Improv Level 2 shows you how to make your improvised scenes and songs look and feel more like a Broadway musical! Exercises in listening and emotional commitment will give you the solid scene-work you need to launch into songs. Also, you will explore different song styles, learning about want songs, philosophy songs, charm songs, and metaphor songs. 8 weeks of classes followed by a class performance.
Prerequisite: Musical Improv Level One
classes.location: Ripley Grier, 305 W. 38th St, New York

classes.title: Noon Bitness - December 2026
classes.schedule: Mon/Tue/Thu/Fri 12pm-2pm PT · Nov 30 - Dec 18 · 12 classes, 1 show
classes.description:
This class runs 4 days a week (Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday) from noon-2pm for 3 weeks. It's at the WGIS space in Los Angeles.

You pay for the month and come as often as you want/can. Premise improv, reps, game of the scene.

You must have taken four multi-week courses at any long form theater. Like 101-401 at UCB. Or Level 1-3 and Game Drill at WGIS.

classes.title: After-Noon Bitness - November 2026
classes.schedule: Mon/Tue/Thu 2:15pm-4:15pm PT · Nov 30 - Dec 17 · 9 classes, 1 show
classes.description:
This class runs 3 days a week (Monday, Tuesday, Thursday) from 2:15pm-4:15pm for 3 weeks.

It's at the WGIS space in Los Angeles. You pay for the month and come as often as you want/can. Premise improv, reps, game of the scene.

You must have taken four multi-week courses at any long form theater. Like 101-401 at UCB. Or Level 1-3 and Game Drill at WGIS.
classes.location: WGIS Space, 1615 N. Vermont Ave., Los Angeles, CA 90027

classes.title: Dr. Cacky's Improv Cleansing
classes.description:
Is your scene work tired and sluggish? Are you falling back on the same tired choices and characters you always make? Do you need to get back to basics and be playful and strong again? If so, Dr. Cacky's Improv Cleansing is for you. He'll give you the improv equivalent of a high colonic, flushing the toxins of insecurity and indecision out of your system. You'll also receive some personalized feedback!

Recommend at least 6 months experience.

Please note: this workshop is on two consecutive days: Monday and Tuesday.
classes.location: WGIS Studio 2, 1613 N. Vermont Ave., Los Angeles, CA 90027

classes.title: WRITE TO SHOOT: Writing the Short Film Script You’ll Actually Make
classes.description: This 8-week short film writing workshop is designed for you to leave with your perfect script, ready to execute. From pitching, to first drafts, to rewrites and a final table read, this course will break down the script writing process into weekly goals, helping you to DO it and not overthink it. Along the way, the class will discuss many of the practical elements of short film production — including development, prep, production and post production — empowering you to find your path forward and make your film happen.
classes.location: Union Square, 113 University Place, Sixth Floor, New York

classes.title: ONLINE Commercial Auditioning
classes.description: Use your improv skills to advance your career and make money as a commercial actor. In this six-week course, you will get plenty of reps (9+ auditions) with real commercial scripts and learn the tips and tricks to successful auditions. The final class includes a professional evaluation of one of YOUR auditions from a casting director, commercial director, or commercial agent. All teaching & feedback is on an individual basis. Casey will meet you wherever you are on your commercial auditioning journey. Whether you’ve never auditioned or are constantly auditioning, this class has something for you. Entirely online so you can participate from anywhere in the world.
classes.location: Online

classes.title: Writing 6 Auditions
classes.description:
The Writing 6 class is holding actor auditions for their final shows. The actors will be featured in the show run for this class. Current students are invited to audition. We recommend auditioners have completed at least Improv 3 or be part of our Conservatory, Acting, or Improv for Actors programs.

classes.title: Storytelling for Business: The Art of Influence and Connection
classes.level: Storytelling for Business: The Art of Influence and Connection
classes.description:
Most people think storytelling is about being entertaining.

It's not.

It's about connection.

Whether you're speaking to a room full of people, leading a team meeting, interviewing for a job, pitching an idea, or having a difficult conversation, stories help people understand who you are, what you stand for, and why your message matters.

In this two-week workshop, award-winning storyteller and longtime Magnet Theater Storytelling instructor Adam Wade will share practical storytelling tools that can help you become a more confident, authentic, and effective communicator. You'll learn how to identify strong story moments from your own life, structure them in a compelling way, adapt them to different audiences, and use them to build trust, credibility, and connection. Along the way, you'll gain a deeper understanding of what makes people listen, remember, and engage—not just on stage, but in everyday life.

classes.title: Three-Day Intensive Storytelling Level One
classes.description:
Want to learn how to tell a story and connect to people from one of the best storytellers in NYC? Magnet Theater Storytelling Instructor Adam Wade (20-time Moth Story Slam Champion, Creator of the Best Selling Audible Original, You Ought To Know Adam Wade) will teach you how to take personal experiences from your life and create stories that are universal and identifiable for an audience. You'll be blown away at how engaging and relatable your personal stories can be! Whether you're a Moth Slam Champion in the making, a writer seeking to fine-tune your narrative skills, or someone who wants the confidence and ability to get in front of people and be heard -- this class will help.

In this class, you will learn the basic elements of telling a narrative story, how to take a crowd by surprise and make them care, how to be real and truthful on stage, and how to discover and communicate the real meaning behind your experience. Classes will include verbal and written exercises and various techniques and approaches to prepare yourself for a performance of your story.

Just some of the things that you'll get out of the class: a higher level of self-confidence, at least one polished, six-to-eight-minute story -- which could be a Moth Story Slam winner, the beginning of a one-person show or personal essay, and the fundamentals needed to develop future stories.

***Since it is a 3-day intensive class, instead of our typical maximum enrollment of 16 students, we will cap the class at 12 maximum to ensure everyone gets the most out of it.***

classes.title: Musical Improv Conservatory Auditions
classes.description:
The Musical Improv Program is for improvisers who love creating musical scenes, and are excited to use music in their comedy career. The Second City uses songs and musical improv on all of it’s stages, and learning how to do it is a lot of fun! Students who complete this program will graduate with a deeper understanding of musical improv, approached in it’s many forms – in game play, narrative, and written work. The aim is to create improvisers who can execute these skills on a professional stage at The Second City, or anywhere else. Students in this program can expect support, encouragement, and notes to grow by.

LEVELS 1 – 2

The first two levels of the music program focus on demystifying musical improv and it’s many elements, and turning them into executable and performable skills! Game play, making strong vocal and musical choices, song structures and rhyming; building musical scenes with authenticity, and building group songs in a fun and supportive environment. Shows are scheduled at each level, and a retention audition is held at the end of Level 2.

LEVELS 3 – 5

The goal of Levels 3-5 is to give the student a professional level experience of musical improv training. Game play for the audience, styles and genres, and long form narratives will be explored with an eye toward re-improvisation and lyric writing. Each level will have a show, with Level 5 culminating in previews and a four-show run of a musical variety show.

AUDITIONS

Please come dressed comfortably for movement and ready to sing! Walk-ins may be accommodated, but are not guaranteed.

• Prerequisites and Eligibility

A full year of improv training at The Second City is required. We will also consider a year long program at an approved school in conjunction with one Acting class post High School.

classes.schedule: Tuesday and Thursday 7pm-11pm PT · Dec 15 - Dec 17 · 2 sessions
classes.description:
NOTE FOR STUDENTS: Chad’s clown intensives do not operate on levels. Each one involves different games and exercises with a unique point of focus. They can be done in any order by students at any level of experience.

Curious about modern clown work? THE ORIGINAL DISRUPTOR is unlike any comedy class you’ve taken. An exploration of not only how games are created and played, but when it’s time to break all the rules. This two-day intensive explores risk, chaos, subversion, paradox, instability, misdirection and the possibilities that exist on the other side of embarrassment and failure.

“The father of modern clown in LA” - NPR

classes.description:
In this course, you will take an idea from a pitch all the way to a polished draft of your very own half hour comedy pilot, getting feedback at each step as you go through this tough but really rewarding process. We'll talk about elements of a strong comedy pilot concept, character creation, outline structure, and how to write dialogue that sounds like it comes from a human. And we'll do it in a supportive workshop environment where you'll be giving feedback on other projects as you work on your own.

This class will break down the comedy pilot writing process into easily achieved weekly goals. You will leave with a completed draft that you can build on and use as a sample. If writing a pilot feels overwhelming, this is the class for you.

classes.title: Improv for Actors 1
classes.description:
In today’s entertainment industry, improv and the ability to work without a script has become an essential tool not only for rehearsal, but for performance on screen and stage, as well as auditioning. Improv for Actors 1 is for people interested in how to be a better actor. IFA-1 is geared toward both working and post-grad actors who are looking to expand their craft with skills of improvisation. It’s also a great option for people with a theater degree or background in the dramatic arts to have fun with new people in a new environment.

IFA-1 covers the fundamental elements of scene work, creating environment, and scenic transformation. Students acquire skills that can be applied to scripted and non-scripted work. Students become more improvisational in written moments and more confident when they improvise.

Students work on building ensemble, object work, and the essence of a good improvisational scene. Using games, exercises, and other play, students explore relationships, character motivation, and heightening techniques to create compelling scenes and characters purely out of improv.

Improv for Actors 1 is for students with a theater degree, currently enrolled in a full-length collegiate theater program, or have the equivalent amount of professional training and/or experience. Students must submit an acting résumé for consideration to be placed in IFA-1. Please submit a résumé through our online application.

classes.title: Intro to Acting
classes.description:
The Second City Acting Program combines improvisational techniques with a variety of scripted media—including materials from the Second City archive—to help students build the foundations of grounded and compelling acting. Second City’s approach to sketch comedy is deeply rooted in behavior, relationships, character, and emotion.

Over the years, our alumni have applied these principles across stage, film, and television to create performances that are not only hilarious but also heartwarming, dramatic, and award-winning. In this course, students will explore core acting techniques and methods for working with scripts.

It’s a great fit for improvisers looking to refine their acting skills or for actors with little to no improv experience who want to stretch their creative muscles and expand their toolbox.

Prerequisites: While some prior improv training is recommended, it is not required.

classes.description:
AP1: Chicago Improv for Beginners

AP1 is an all-encompassing survey course that will give anyone a solid foundation in improvisational comedy – whether you want to perform, direct, write, or just know more.

New to improv? This class is for you. AP1 introduces you to Chicago's approach to improv by covering a wide variety of concepts:​

• The rules of Improv and breaking the rules
• Group mind (the myth, the facts)
• How to say "yes, and" and when to say “no”
• Finding or Creating the game
• Long-form
• Short-form
• Writing via improv
• Direction (taking and giving)
• Object and environment work
• Introducing a show

This class will culminate in an optional student showcase at The Annoyance on the final Sunday of the term.

Prerequisite: None
classes.location: 851 W Belmont Ave, Chicago, IL

classes.title: AP2 - Mondays with TBD T127
classes.description:
AP2: Beginning Annoyance Philosophy - Initiations

AP2 is an immersive examination of The Annoyance philosophy on, and approach to, improv. AP2 focuses on decisive initiations and a strong point of view. This class focuses on the first seconds of scenes and explores how they affect the rest of the scene.

In AP2, you will cover:

• Personal responsibility in a scene − taking care of yourself and your choices
• Trusting instincts
• Creating/Finding “Your Deal” at the top of the scene
• Beginning character development
• Object work as inspiration
• Environment as inspiration
• The responsibility of operating without censorship.
• Individual feedback and tendencies

This class will culminate in an optional student showcase at The Annoyance on the final Sunday of the term.

Prerequisite:
AP1 or sufficient background in improv. Please let us know in the comments section below where you have studied so that we may contact them to confirm.
classes.location: 851 W Belmont Ave, Chicago, IL

classes.title: AP3 - Mondays withTBD T127
classes.description:
AP3: Scene Work

AP3 is about taking that next step in scenes. While AP2 focused on the beginning moments of a scene, in AP3 students are challenged to play with more complexity and style, juggling it all within a scene while always maintaining their strong point of view.

Aspects of this class include:

• Acknowledging the realities of your scene partner
• Scenic development: Finding the Highways and Bi-ways of a scene to extend its length
• Managing context without getting in your head (the who/what/where/when/why/etc.)
• Creating specific, surprising choices
• Playing with Opposites and Curve Balls
• Creating and playing with multiple patterns or games in a scene
• In-depth three person and group scene work
• Protecting and Playing the Freak
• Learning how to repair a scene that isn’t working
• Managing forms and style
• DaDa scenes (playing fiercely without needing to “make sense”)
• Justification: how to use it not out of fear but as a tool.
• Personal challenge and goals based on individual feedback

Prerequisite:
Students must have completed AP2 to take this course.
classes.location: 851 W Belmont Ave, Chicago, IL

classes.title: AP4 - Mondays with TBD T127
classes.description:
AP4

Through individual feedback, setting performance goals, and identifying and breaking habits, AP4 offers fine-tuning and involves the following aspects:

• Stretching the performer
• Pushing unique specificity
• Keeping voice in multiple person scenes, split-scenes
• Making rich, varied environments
• Embodying the character and embellishing the world
• Organic improv ∼ developing a scene based on physical and emotional choices

Prerequisite:
Students must have completed AP3 to take this class.

classes.title: Advanced Study Performance: The Convergence
classes.schedule: Mondays 7pm-10pm ET · Jan 4 - Feb 23 · 8 sessions + class show
classes.description:
Worlds collide in The Convergence. Two unrelated monoscenes unfold until deeper connections emerge, and their actions begin to influence each other. What might seem like two ordinary scenes is something more.

A struggling author writing his latest novel. Monkeys escaping from a zoo. The monkeys found a room of typewriters and they’re putting the author out of business.

Nuns completing their daily routines. A pie factory about to shut down. We learn the nuns worship a pie-based religion based on four brave factory workers who sacrificed themselves to keep pie alive.

Four friends having a fancy dinner. Lawyers interviewing their clients. The four friends are the lice on the lawyer’s head. Think about it.

In two back-and-forth monologues that slowly dissolve, we learn that nothing is what it seems.

Class shows will take place on the Mainstage

This class is application based, please apply before: December 2nd.

Applications will close EOD on 12/2. Those accepted into the class will be notified on or before December 9th.

There is no additional application form, just click register and enter your name and email to submit an application.

This class will help remind you what you love about improv, slap you out of whatever may be holding you back, and cut out the naysaying voices in your head. We will look at how we sometimes bail on our choices out of a fear of making the “right or wrong choice” and to instead approach improv with a “fuck it/love it” mentality (because improv is one of the most wonderful things in the world if you don’t treat it too seriously). This class encourages your artistic freedom with methods to initiate scenes with an emotional point of view, to be specific and surprising in your choices, to support your scene partner, and to confidently navigate the vocabulary and concepts of long-form improv. This class will move quickly, keep you on your feet, and challenge you with personal feedback.

classes.description:
Writing 1 is for any student who is looking to start the journey of writing to and for a Second City-style revue. This class is the foundation for scenic comedy writing, a guide for utilizing an improviser’s skill set for rapid creation, and learning writing refinement. The concepts and tools provided in Writing 1 are the building blocks for being able to quickly and creatively write to and for a Second City-style revue. Every comedic writer must have the knowledge and skills that are offered in this course.

Writing 1 teaches students how to write comedic scenes that could be found in a Second City-style revue by exploring different scenic set-ups, character dialogue, genres and point-of-view. Students use improv as a tool for character and dialogue generation.

Writing 1 class time includes a combination of solo exercises and collaborative exercises to build skills in brainstorming, comedic structure and character development. Students also gain a Second City perspective on theatrical writing – including observation, idea generation, dialogue, and character creation. Feedback focuses on ‘what works’ in terms of the structural building blocks. Class time is active, positive and encouraging. Students practice concepts through a series of weekly homework assignments.

Any student interested in creating Second City-style comedic writing or interested in extending their improvisation abilities and experiences into writing should take Writing 1.
classes.location: Second City Training Center, 230 W. North Ave, Chicago

classes.title: iO Improv Level 1: Mondays from 7-10pm
classes.description:
Level 1 introduces students to all of the concepts necessary to become adept improvisers and performers. Students will learn how to build and apply the basic fundamentals of improvisation through a series of exercises, games, and storytelling. Level 1 is the appropriate starting point for the inexperienced student, but even those with some improv or theater experience will find value in the lessons of Level 1. The class will culminate in students learning and performing iO's signature piece, The Harold, one of the most sophisticated and rewarding forms of pure improv ever created.

While 'Yes, And' is the guiding ethos in improvisation, students will go above and beyond that simple principle and learn how acceptance, agreement, honesty, connections, listening, and commitment will help them discover the truth in comedy. Our expert instructors foster a safe and joyous environment for students to play, experiment, and relish in the experimentation of improv.

Level 1 is an 8-week course that meets once a week for 3 hours. At the end of the term, each class will have a short 10-minute performance demonstration open to the public.
classes.location: 1501 N. Kingsbury St., Chicago, IL 60642

classes.title: iO Improv Level 2: Mondays from 7-10pm
classes.description:
Level 2 expands upon the principles explored in Level 1 and teaches students the skills to make strong, bold and committed choices to elevate their characters, scenes, and performances. This level focuses on the importance of creating something artful and beautifully compelling on stage, challenging students to be more than just talking heads in their improvisation. Students will be engaged in exercises that encourage them to use physicality, environment, and stage picture to inspire their improvisation and raise the status of their improv from simple games and scenes to high performance art.

The principles of Level 2 separate iO's training center from other improv schools by focusing on bold decision making and group support. Students will work together to commit to each other's choices and elevate those choices, creating truly unique and inspiring moments of improvisation.

Level 2 is an 8-week course that meets once a week for 3 hours. At the end of the term, each class will have a short 10-minute performance demonstration open to the public.
classes.location: 1501 N. Kingsbury St., Chicago, IL 60642

classes.title: iO Improv Level 3: Mondays from 7-10pm
classes.description:
Level 3 redirects the focus back on to the essential building block of longform improvisation, the two person scene. The exercises in this level will help students slow down and find grounded real points of view and relationships to explore in their scenes. Rather than act like cartoon characters, Level 3 helps students understand that by listening and reacting to what someone is saying to them, they can create compelling and emotional scenes that will naturally evolve into comedy. Students will learn to develop the natural instincts that will help their scenes flourish and connect with audiences and will receive individualized feedback from their instructor about their strengths and opportunities for growth.

'Every line is golden and every detail is golden.' The principles of Level 3 help reassure students that they already have everything they need to create a great scene. Students will stop "inventing" and start truly improvising with guidance on how to respond with real emotions and committed character choices.

Level 3 is an 8-week course that meets once a week for 3 hours. At the end of the term, each class will have a short 10-minute performance demonstration open to the public.
classes.location: 1501 N. Kingsbury St., Chicago, IL 60642

classes.title: iO Improv Level 4: Mondays from 7-10pm
classes.description:
Level 4 synthesizes the lessons from all of the previous levels and allows students to begin creating longform pieces that are cohesive, thoughtful, and artistic. Students will learn a variety of classic longform pieces in an effort to understand how structure can inform their art. Each form taught will offer students an opportunity to learn how a form can be a motivator of creativity and authenticity, and not just a rigid structure to adhere to. The skills in this class will help students perform longer sets and will encourage true improvisational exploration of ideas, concepts, and thoughts–urging students to actually say something with their art.

Learn the rules, obey the rules, then break the rules. Additional focus will be given to iO's signature longform style, The Harold. Developed and performed at iO for the last 35 years, the Harold is now taught and performed all over the world and is a sophisticated and rewarding form that lends itself to all styles of improvisation. Students will learn the intricacies of performing the Harold with the understanding that the form is just a launching point for inspiration and not a destination in and of itself.

Level 4 is an 8-week course that meets once a week for 3 hours. At the end of the term, each class will have a short 10-minute performance demonstration open to the public.
classes.location: 1501 N. Kingsbury St., Chicago, IL 60642

classes.title: iO Improv Level 5: Mondays from 7-10pm
classes.description:
This level is the culminating class of the iO program and is followed by an 8-week run of performances on Sunday nights from January 10th, 2027 through February 28th, 2027, for which you do not pay tuition.

Level 5 pushes students into a true ensemble mindset and challenges the groups to create their own unique longform piece. Inspired by their work in Level 4 and all the previous levels, students will work together under the guidance and assistance of their instructor to brainstorm and generate a new, unique form that will be performed on stage. This level allows for a lot of personalized notes and diagnostics from the instructor and really helps students grow as individuals while also operating in an ensemble state of mind.

At the end of this 8 week course, the students will spend the following 8 weeks performing their devised piece on stage at iO every Sunday night. Following the completion of level 5 and their performances, all iO graduates will be eligible to audition for the House Team program at iO, allowing them to continue their education and perform on a coached ensemble with weekly rehearsals and semi-weekly shows, sponsored by the theater.
classes.location: 1501 N. Kingsbury St., Chicago, IL 60642

classes.description: From day one you will jump into a series of fun warm ups and games designed to ease you into improv. As the class progresses you will learn how to do 2 person scenes, group scenes, group games and how to deliver simple monologues. The class is all about fun and support. Whether you are a beginner who has never improvised or someone who has improv experience, you will learn strong fundamentals that will build your confidence, improve speaking skills and foster spontaneity

classes.title: Storytelling Level One
classes.description:
Want to learn how to tell a story and connect to people from one of the best storytellers in NYC? Magnet Theater Storytelling Instructor Adam Wade (20-time Moth Story Slam Champion, Creator of the Best Selling Audible Original, You Ought To Know Adam Wade) will teach you how to take personal experiences from your life and create stories that are universal and identifiable for an audience. You'll be blown away at how engaging and relatable your personal stories can be! Whether you're a Moth Slam Champion in the making, a writer seeking to fine-tune your narrative skills, or someone who wants the confidence and ability to get in front of people and be heard -- this class will help.

In this class, you will learn the basic elements of telling a narrative story, how to take a crowd by surprise and make them care, how to be real and truthful on stage, and how to discover and communicate the real meaning behind your experience. Classes will include verbal and written exercises and various techniques and approaches to prepare yourself for a performance of your story.

Just some of the things that you'll get out of the class: a higher level of self-confidence, at least one polished, five-to-six-minute story -- which could be a Moth Story Slam winner, the beginning of a one-person show or personal essay, and the fundamentals needed to develop future stories.

The class concludes with a graduation performance where you will perform your personal story in front of a live, super-supportive audience!

Since 2010, Adam has helped over 3,500 students with their own stories in these Storytelling Classes at Magnet Theater.

classes.title: AP1 - Tuesdays with TBD T127
classes.description:
AP1: Chicago Improv for Beginners

AP1 is an all-encompassing survey course that will give anyone a solid foundation in improvisational comedy – whether you want to perform, direct, write, or just know more.

New to improv? This class is for you. AP1 introduces you to Chicago's approach to improv by covering a wide variety of concepts:​

• The rules of Improv and breaking the rules
• Group mind (the myth, the facts)
• How to say "yes, and" and when to say “no”
• Finding or Creating the game
• Long-form
• Short-form
• Writing via improv
• Direction (taking and giving)
• Object and environment work
• Introducing a show

This class will culminate in an optional student showcase at The Annoyance on the final Sunday of the term.

Prerequisite: None
classes.location: 851 W Belmont Ave, Chicago, IL

classes.title: AP2 - Tuesdays with Megan Johns T127
classes.description:
AP2: Beginning Annoyance Philosophy - Initiations

AP2 is an immersive examination of The Annoyance philosophy on, and approach to, improv. AP2 focuses on decisive initiations and a strong point of view. This class focuses on the first seconds of scenes and explores how they affect the rest of the scene.

In AP2, you will cover:

• Personal responsibility in a scene − taking care of yourself and your choices
• Trusting instincts
• Creating/Finding “Your Deal” at the top of the scene
• Beginning character development
• Object work as inspiration
• Environment as inspiration
• The responsibility of operating without censorship.
• Individual feedback and tendencies

This class will culminate in an optional student showcase at The Annoyance on the final Sunday of the term.

Prerequisite:
AP1 or sufficient background in improv. Please let us know in the comments section below where you have studied so that we may contact them to confirm.
classes.location: 851 W Belmont Ave, Chicago, IL

classes.title: AP3 - Tuesdays withTBD T127
classes.description:
AP3: Scene Work

AP3 is about taking that next step in scenes. While AP2 focused on the beginning moments of a scene, in AP3 students are challenged to play with more complexity and style, juggling it all within a scene while always maintaining their strong point of view.

Aspects of this class include:

• Acknowledging the realities of your scene partner
• Scenic development: Finding the Highways and Bi-ways of a scene to extend its length
• Managing context without getting in your head (the who/what/where/when/why/etc.)
• Creating specific, surprising choices
• Playing with Opposites and Curve Balls
• Creating and playing with multiple patterns or games in a scene
• In-depth three person and group scene work
• Protecting and Playing the Freak
• Learning how to repair a scene that isn’t working
• Managing forms and style
• DaDa scenes (playing fiercely without needing to “make sense”)
• Justification: how to use it not out of fear but as a tool.
• Personal challenge and goals based on individual feedback

Prerequisite:
Students must have completed AP2 to take this course.
classes.location: 851 W Belmont Ave, Chicago, IL

classes.title: CRASS2 - Tuesdays with TBD T127
classes.description:
CRASS2: Sketch To Narrative Play

CRASS (CReating Annoyance Style Shows) is a the next step in The Annoyance's process; using improv to create written material.

In CRASS 2, students will take the skills they learned in CRASS 1, (how to turn their improv into written sketches), and further develop their work with the creation of a narrative play. As in CRASS 1, students will be assigned roles and be responsible for costumes, props, etc. Additional work outside of class will be required.

For over 30 years the Annoyance has specialized in using improv comedy to create full length plays and musicals. From Annoyance classics like Splatter Theater and Coed Prison Sluts, to more modern shows like Steamworks: The Musical, Live Laugh Blood, and It's Christmas, Goddamnit! The Annoyance has enjoyed pushing the envelope of what plays and musicals can be.

With this class, students will continue their journey of turning their improv into written works, now adding the complexity of a narrative play through it all.

• Using Annoyance style improvisation to build a narrative show
• Theatre Roles
• Technical aspects of the theatre

Prerequisite:
Students must have completed CRASS 1 to enroll in this class

Tech:
This class will feature a tech rehearsal on Sunday 3/21 1-4pm

Shows:
This class will culminate in a run of four shows on Sundays 3/21 - 4/11 7pm

classes.description:
Clown. The great equalizer.

"It's you, of course, the clown. And that's important." -Nader Farman

Clown trains us to be fully present. Class curriculum includes exercises from Jacques Lecoq, Jean Taylor, Merry Conway, Nader Farman, Keith Johnstone and more, aiming to move us past ego and toward our shared humanity. Winter is coming. But class is joyful and warm! Come on out, try on the red nose.

Recognize the universal shared experience that is clowning.

This class culminates in a public class performance.

classes.description:
In this class, you will learn that anything can be the clown's script.

We will build on the skills learned in Level 1, leaning into the most vulnerable parts of yourself and heightening them to a ridiculous extent. You’ll learn that anything can be the clown’s script, lean into the most vulnerable parts of ourselves and heighten them. You’ll identify pieces of yourself and find ways to explore them that are both loving and silly. By the end, you will have the tools to begin building your own clown show.

Through your relationship to everything, you are the clown.

classes.title: Improv Level 2: Free Your Mind w/ Hannah Rehak (Jan-Feb '27) (Tuesday)
classes.description:
Love what’s happening onstage and you’re bound to have fun and fearless improvisation.

This class will help remind you what you love about improv, slap you out of whatever may be holding you back, and cut out the naysaying voices in your head. We will look at how we sometimes bail on our choices out of a fear of making the “right or wrong choice" and to instead approach improv with a "fuck it / love it" mentality (because improv is one of the most wonderful things in the world if you don't treat it too seriously). This class encourages your artistic freedom with methods to initiate scenes with an emotional point of view, to be specific and surprising in your choices, to support your scene partner, and to confidently navigate the vocabulary and concepts of long-form improv. This class will move quickly, keep you on your feet, and challenge you with personal feedback.

This class culminates in a performance for the public.

Prerequisite: Completion of BCC Level 1 Improv OR students who have taken at least one full-length course at a major comedy theater (UCB, PIT, Magnet, Squirrel, Second City, iO, Annoyance, etc.) or have similar prior training can begin at this level. classes.description:
This class builds on the skills in Level 2, teaching students to be versatile ensemble players who can build long-form pieces organically while keeping the show and audience's experience in mind. By layering more complicated improv techniques and awareness onto already fearless play, students will learn how to authentically ground characters so they feel believable and use curve balls to keep scenes surprising. We’ll explore the dynamics that make up three-person and group scenes and how to augment and balance multiple points of focus onstage. And we’ll learn to stay out of our heads while balancing it all.

In addition to learning advanced techniques, this class will encourage you to lean into the areas you shy away from and own what makes you unique as a performer through personal notes and individual challenges.

Improv to Sketch Comedy 1 introduces you to the tools and techniques needed to master basic sketch structures while embracing ensemble and collaborative idea generation through improv!

Over the course of 8 weeks, you will learn how to pitch, write, and perform in sketches, culminating in a staged reading at an end-of-session- showcase where you will present some of your classwork. By working as an ensemble, the class will pitch scene ideas, improvise through them, and ultimately turn that into written sketches. Students who complete this level will be able to collaboratively generate and write sketches in multiple foundational structures!

classes.description:
This class is for anyone interested in learning the process of writing sketch comedy. Throughout the seven-week course, we will discuss, practice, and polish scenes that will culminate in a staged show. Each week will focus on one specific part of the sketch comedy world. These include creating through improv, finding the “game” of a sketch, writing characters, and more! Why do we love certain sketches? How does one go about writing a character? How do we create something from a blank page? Questions like these will be explored in a positive, low stakes/high fun environment. There is no magic key to unlocking great sketch comedy, but this introductory class will help beginning writers find some doors and start knocking.

The intensive will include 18 hours of class over 5 days, broken up into 4 days from 12-4pm and 12-2pm on Sunday. classes.title: Writing 1
classes.description:
Writing 1 is for any student who is looking to start the journey of writing to and for a Second City-style revue. This class is the foundation for scenic comedy writing, a guide for utilizing an improviser’s skill set for rapid creation, and learning writing refinement. The concepts and tools provided in Writing 1 are the building blocks for being able to quickly and creatively write to and for a Second City-style revue. Every comedic writer must have the knowledge and skills that are offered in this course.

Writing 1 teaches students how to write comedic scenes that could be found in a Second City-style revue by exploring different scenic set-ups, character dialogue, genres and point-of-view. Students use improv as a tool for character and dialogue generation.

Writing 1 class time includes a combination of solo exercises and collaborative exercises to build skills in brainstorming, comedic structure and character development. Students also gain a Second City perspective on theatrical writing – including observation, idea generation, dialogue, and character creation. Feedback focuses on ‘what works’ in terms of the structural building blocks. Class time is active, positive and encouraging. Students practice concepts through a series of weekly homework assignments.

Any student interested in creating Second City-style comedic writing or interested in extending their improvisation abilities and experiences into writing should take Writing 1.

classes.title: AP1 - Wednesdays with TBD T127
classes.description:
AP1: Chicago Improv for Beginners

AP1 is an all-encompassing survey course that will give anyone a solid foundation in improvisational comedy – whether you want to perform, direct, write, or just know more.

New to improv? This class is for you. AP1 introduces you to Chicago's approach to improv by covering a wide variety of concepts:​

• The rules of Improv and breaking the rules
• Group mind (the myth, the facts)
• How to say "yes, and" and when to say “no”
• Finding or Creating the game
• Long-form
• Short-form
• Writing via improv
• Direction (taking and giving)
• Object and environment work
• Introducing a show

This class will culminate in an optional student showcase at The Annoyance on the final Sunday of the term.

Prerequisite: None
classes.location: 851 W Belmont Ave, Chicago, IL

classes.title: AP2 - Wednesdays with Casey Alltop T127
classes.description:
AP2: Beginning Annoyance Philosophy - Initiations

AP2 is an immersive examination of The Annoyance philosophy on, and approach to, improv. AP2 focuses on decisive initiations and a strong point of view. This class focuses on the first seconds of scenes and explores how they affect the rest of the scene.

In AP2, you will cover:

• Personal responsibility in a scene − taking care of yourself and your choices
• Trusting instincts
• Creating/Finding “Your Deal” at the top of the scene
• Beginning character development
• Object work as inspiration
• Environment as inspiration
• The responsibility of operating without censorship.
• Individual feedback and tendencies

This class will culminate in an optional student showcase at The Annoyance on the final Sunday of the term.

Prerequisite:
AP1 or sufficient background in improv. Please let us know in the comments section below where you have studied so that we may contact them to confirm.
classes.location: 851 W Belmont Ave, Chicago, IL

classes.title: AP3 - Wednesdays withTBD T127
classes.description:
AP3: Scene Work

AP3 is about taking that next step in scenes. While AP2 focused on the beginning moments of a scene, in AP3 students are challenged to play with more complexity and style, juggling it all within a scene while always maintaining their strong point of view.

Aspects of this class include:

• Acknowledging the realities of your scene partner
• Scenic development: Finding the Highways and Bi-ways of a scene to extend its length
• Managing context without getting in your head (the who/what/where/when/why/etc.)
• Creating specific, surprising choices
• Playing with Opposites and Curve Balls
• Creating and playing with multiple patterns or games in a scene
• In-depth three person and group scene work
• Protecting and Playing the Freak
• Learning how to repair a scene that isn’t working
• Managing forms and style
• DaDa scenes (playing fiercely without needing to “make sense”)
• Justification: how to use it not out of fear but as a tool.
• Personal challenge and goals based on individual feedback

Prerequisite:
Students must have completed AP2 to take this course.
classes.location: 851 W Belmont Ave, Chicago, IL

classes.title: AP4 - Wednesdays with Bruce Phillips T127
classes.description:
AP4

Through individual feedback, setting performance goals, and identifying and breaking habits, AP4 offers fine-tuning and involves the following aspects:

• Stretching the performer
• Pushing unique specificity
• Keeping voice in multiple person scenes, split-scenes
• Making rich, varied environments
• Embodying the character and embellishing the world
• Organic improv ∼ developing a scene based on physical and emotional choices

Prerequisite:
Students must have completed AP3 to take this class.

classes.title: AP5 - Wednesdays with Lauren Rivas T127

AP5 focuses on the creation of an original improv show inspired and devised by the ensemble. Exercises are tailored to help the improviser discover and strengthen their individual comedic improv voice and also on the “hows” of bringing this voice into an ensemble. The class also will delve into the improv rehearsal process and work with the concepts of ensemble building, collaboration, show pacing, and good rehearsal habits.

Love what’s happening onstage and you’re bound to have fun and fearless improvisation.

This class will help remind you what you love about improv, slap you out of whatever may be holding you back, and cut out the naysaying voices in your head. We will look at how we sometimes bail on our choices out of a fear of making the “right or wrong choice" and to instead approach improv with a "fuck it / love it" mentality (because improv is one of the most wonderful things in the world if you don't treat it too seriously). This class encourages your artistic freedom with methods to initiate scenes with an emotional point of view, to be specific and surprising in your choices, to support your scene partner, and to confidently navigate the vocabulary and concepts of long-form improv.
