classes.title: iO Improv Level 1: Wednesdays from 7-10pm
classes.description:
Level 1 introduces students to all of the concepts necessary to become adept improvisers and performers. Students will learn how to build and apply the basic fundamentals of improvisation through a series of exercises, games, and storytelling. Level 1 is the appropriate starting point for the inexperienced student, but even those with some improv or theater experience will find value in the lessons of Level 1. The class will culminate in students learning and performing iO's signature piece, The Harold, one of the most sophisticated and rewarding forms of pure improv ever created.

While 'Yes, And' is the guiding ethos in improvisation, students will go above and beyond that simple principle and learn how acceptance, agreement, honesty, connections, listening, and commitment will help them discover the truth in comedy. Our expert instructors foster a safe and joyous environment for students to play, experiment, and relish in the experimentation of improv.

Level 1 is an 8-week course that meets once a week for 3 hours. At the end of the term, each class will have a short 10-minute performance demonstration open to the public.
classes.location: 1501 N. Kingsbury St., Chicago, IL 60642

classes.title: iO Improv Level 2: Wednesdays from 7-10pm
classes.description:
Level 2 expands upon the principles explored in Level 1 and teaches students the skills to make strong, bold and committed choices to elevate their characters, scenes, and performances. This level focuses on the importance of creating something artful and beautifully compelling on stage, challenging students to be more than just talking heads in their improvisation. Students will be engaged in exercises that encourage them to use physicality, environment, and stage picture to inspire their improvisation and raise the status of their improv from simple games and scenes to high performance art.

The principles of Level 2 separate iO's training center from other improv schools by focusing on bold decision making and group support. Students will work together to commit to each other's choices and elevate those choices, creating truly unique and inspiring moments of improvisation.

Level 2 is an 8-week course that meets once a week for 3 hours. At the end of the term, each class will have a short 10-minute performance demonstration open to the public.
classes.location: 1501 N. Kingsbury St., Chicago, IL 60642

classes.title: iO Improv Level 3: Wednesdays from 7-10pm
classes.description:
Level 3 redirects the focus back on to the essential building block of longform improvisation, the two person scene. The exercises in this level will help students slow down and find grounded real points of view and relationships to explore in their scenes. Rather than act like cartoon characters, Level 3 helps students understand that by listening and reacting to what someone is saying to them, they can create compelling and emotional scenes that will naturally evolve into comedy. Students will learn to develop the natural instincts that will help their scenes flourish and connect with audiences and will receive individualized feedback from their instructor about their strengths and opportunities for growth.

'Every line is golden and every detail is golden.' The principles of Level 3 help reassure students that they already have everything they need to create a great scene. Students will stop "inventing" and start truly improvising with guidance on how to respond with real emotions and committed character choices.

Level 3 is an 8-week course that meets once a week for 3 hours. At the end of the term, each class will have a short 10-minute performance demonstration open to the public.
classes.location: 1501 N. Kingsbury St., Chicago, IL 60642

classes.title: iO Improv Level 4: Wednesdays from 7-10pm
classes.description:
Level 4 synthesizes the lessons from all of the previous levels and allows students to begin creating longform pieces that are cohesive, thoughtful, and artistic. Students will learn a variety of classic longform pieces in an effort to understand how structure can inform their art. Each form taught will offer students an opportunity to learn how a form can be a motivator of creativity and authenticity, and not just a rigid structure to adhere to. The skills in this class will help students perform longer sets and will encourage true improvisational exploration of ideas, concepts, and thoughts–urging students to actually say something with their art.

Learn the rules, obey the rules, then break the rules. Additional focus will be given to iO's signature longform style, The Harold. Developed and performed at iO for the last 35 years, the Harold is now taught and performed all over the world and is a sophisticated and rewarding form that lends itself to all styles of improvisation. Students will learn the intricacies of performing the Harold with the understanding that the form is just a launching point for inspiration and not a destination in and of itself.

Level 4 is an 8-week course that meets once a week for 3 hours. At the end of the term, each class will have a short 10-minute performance demonstration open to the public.
classes.location: 1501 N. Kingsbury St., Chicago, IL 60642

classes.title: iO Improv Level 5: Wednesdays from 7-10pm
classes.description:
This level is the culminating class of the iO program and is followed by an 8-week run of performances on Sunday nights from January 10th, 2027 through February 28th, 2027, for which you do not pay tuition.

Level 5 pushes students into a true ensemble mindset and challenges the groups to create their own unique longform piece. Inspired by their work in Level 4 and all the previous levels, students will work together under the guidance and assistance of their instructor to brainstorm and generate a new, unique form that will be performed on stage. This level allows for a lot of personalized notes and diagnostics from the instructor and really helps students grow as individuals while also operating in an ensemble state of mind.

At the end of this 8 week course, the students will spend the following 8 weeks performing their devised piece on stage at iO every Sunday night. Following the completion of level 5 and their performances, all iO graduates will be eligible to audition for the House Team program at iO, allowing them to continue their education and perform on a coached ensemble with weekly rehearsals and semi-weekly shows, sponsored by the theater.

Intro to Writing for TV & Film is for anyone who wants to learn the crucial basics of writing for film and television or anyone with a great idea of a movie who needs help putting it into (properly formatted) words. It gives you a strong foundation for TV and film writing, demystifies the language and process of writing, and gives you the tools to begin turning your great idea into the next Citizen Kane/Troop Beverly Hills (same thing).

You’ll learn about the language of film/TV writing, the importance of deadlines, the unique qualities of a cinematic story versus a sketch, lots of screenplay formatting, how and what to pitch, and the scale of your ideas.

You’ll watch films and TV shows with a critical ear for dialogue and structure, read scripts, learn how to pitch, pitch those great ideas, and create outlines or treatments for that million-dollar sitcom or film idea. Oh, and table reads!

This course is a great introduction to the Comedy TV Pilots and Writing for Late Night programs.

• Creating and playing with multiple patterns or games in a scene
• In-depth three person and group scene work
• Protecting and Playing the Freak
• Learning how to repair a scene that isn’t working
• Managing forms and style
• DaDa scenes (playing fiercely without needing to “make sense”)
• Justification: how to use it not out of fear but as a tool.
• Personal challenge and goals based on individual feedback

Students must have completed AP2 to take this course.

classes.title: AP4 - Thursdays with Ross Taylor T127
classes.description:
AP4

Through individual feedback, setting performance goals, and identifying and breaking habits, AP4 offers fine-tuning and involves the following aspects:

• Stretching the performer
• Pushing unique specificity
• Keeping voice in multiple person scenes, split-scenes
• Making rich, varied environments
• Embodying the character and embellishing the world
• Organic improv ∼ developing a scene based on physical and emotional choices

Prerequisite:
Students must have completed AP3 to take this class.
classes.location: 851 W Belmont Ave, Chicago, IL

classes.title: MI1 - Thursdays with Brody Lemke and Karen Sandvoss T127
classes.description:
MI1: Scene Into Song

Musical Improv I is an introduction to improvising songs, and the art of 'scene into song'. You'll learn how to sing structured songs, create catchy choruses that audiences remember, how to dance the same improvised dance move with seven other people, and how to express honest emotion while getting big laughs. This class will culminate in a one-night-only Musical Improv
class show.

YOU DO NOT HAVE TO BE A GOOD SINGER TO BE A GREAT MUSICAL IMPROVISER! All you need is a supportive teacher to help you through the first few anxiety-ridden moments. I was never in choir growing up, and didn't think of myself as a 'singer'--I heard the vibrato of Broadway voices and thought 'I'm DEFINITELY not a singer. 'But it turns out I'm a GREAT singer--I just needed to improvise a few hundred songs to get VERY comfortable with my own voice. So whether you're interested in musical improv, or just want to feel more confident with your own voice, this class is for you.

Prerequisite:
Students must have completed AP3 or at least two improv classes at any theatre

classes.description:
Clown. The great equalizer.

"It's you, of course, the clown. And that's important." -Nader Farman

Clown trains us to be fully present. Class curriculum includes exercises from Jacques Lecoq, Jean Taylor, Merry Conway, Nader Farman, Keith Johnstone and more, aiming to move us past ego and toward our shared humanity. Winter is coming. But class is joyful and warm! Come on out, try on the red nose.

Recognize the universal shared experience that is clowning.

This class culminates in a public class performance.

classes.title: Clown Level 3: Ensemble w/ Jeff Seal (Jan-Feb '27) (Thursday)
classes.description:
You’ve started getting laughs as a clown but now how do you do it 6 days a week and twice on Saturdays for an audience that’s never even heard of clowning? In this class we’ll take the skills you learned in Clown 1 and 2 honing your clown persona and learn to create working acts as part of a fully realized show, collaboratively created by the ensemble.

How does your clown solve a problem? How do you work as a company? What's the world you're going to set up with lots of clowns?

You will further build your clown character by finding a costume that makes you look and feel stupid and start creating material by finding your own stupid clown logic. We’ll also explore “le jeu” and status in clown duos and trios, as well as building a thematic world that ties the whole show together. Come to class with ideas, costumes, props or anything that ignites your imagination. Students should be prepared to rehearse as they would in a professional ensemble process - with homework prepped outside of class and attending classes and the tech rehearsal on-time and present.

This class culminates in two class shows on the Eris MainStage

Students learn to recognize patterns and comedic themes within scenes and how to heighten these elements for maximum comedic impact. Students will also be introduced to new concepts such as editing, second beats, and more. Take the next step in your improv journey with 201!

Building upon and utilizing the skills from our previous levels, students will find game in their scenes and learn how to connect these scenes into one cohesive piece - The Harold. Students will have the opportunity to learn one to two brand new openings and perform each in a class show.

This level provides an additional class show, midway, and more individualized feedback from your instructor! If passed by your instructor, students will be eligible to take Advanced Study Courses. The learning doesn’t have to stop here!

classes.description:
First time taking an improv class? You’re in the right place.

This class will introduce new improvisers to the value of saying “Yes, and” to every idea (especially their own) to become joyful, fearless, and bold performers. Through games and exercises this class will teach students to react emotionally and honestly, to trust your gut, to support scene partners and embrace taking risks. These skills are essential to successful improvisation! Whether you want to be a performer or try out a class to meet new people, this class is bound to boost your confidence and creativity in a safe and supportive environment.

This class culminates in a performance for the public.

classes.title: Improv Level 2: Free Your Mind w/ Devin Bockrath (Jan-Feb '27) (Thursday)
classes.description:
Love what’s happening onstage and you’re bound to have fun and fearless improvisation.

This class will help remind you what you love about improv, slap you out of whatever may be holding you back, and cut out the naysaying voices in your head. We will look at how we sometimes bail on our choices out of a fear of making the “right or wrong choice" and to instead approach improv with a "fuck it / love it" mentality (because improv is one of the most wonderful things in the world if you don't treat it too seriously). This class encourages your artistic freedom with methods to initiate scenes with an emotional point of view, to be specific and surprising in your choices, to support your scene partner, and to confidently navigate the vocabulary and concepts of long-form improv. This class will move quickly, keep you on your feet, and challenge you with personal feedback.

This class culminates in a performance for the public.

classes.description:
After Level 1, you will have learned all the basic tools you need to do musical improv. Level 2 will delve more deeply into technique to fine tune your skills. We'll be going deep into effective scene work, strategic gifting, complex song structures, confident characters, rapping and rhyming, nailing genre, improved musicality, and polished choreography. This class will push you to grow and prepare you for higher quality shows, all while having tons of silly fun.

By focusing on each individual’s strengths, this course will focus on how to craft a clean set, host and put together a show, and develop tricks to solidify your own voice.

classes.title: iO Improv Level 1: Thursdays from 7-10pm
classes.description:
Level 1 introduces students to all of the concepts necessary to become adept improvisers and performers. Students will learn how to build and apply the basic fundamentals of improvisation through a series of exercises, games, and storytelling. Level 1 is the appropriate starting point for the inexperienced student, but even those with some improv or theater experience will find value in the lessons of Level 1. The class will culminate in students learning and performing iO's signature piece, The Harold, one of the most sophisticated and rewarding forms of pure improv ever created.

While 'Yes, And' is the guiding ethos in improvisation, students will go above and beyond that simple principle and learn how acceptance, agreement, honesty, connections, listening, and commitment will help them discover the truth in comedy. Our expert instructors foster a safe and joyous environment for students to play, experiment, and relish in the experimentation of improv.

Level 1 is an 8-week course that meets once a week for 3 hours. At the end of the term, each class will have a short 10-minute performance demonstration open to the public.
classes.location: 1501 N. Kingsbury St., Chicago, IL 60642

classes.title: iO Improv Level 2: Thursdays from 7-10pm
classes.description:
Level 2 expands upon the principles explored in Level 1 and teaches students the skills to make strong, bold and committed choices to elevate their characters, scenes, and performances. This level focuses on the importance of creating something artful and beautifully compelling on stage, challenging students to be more than just talking heads in their improvisation. Students will be engaged in exercises that encourage them to use physicality, environment, and stage picture to inspire their improvisation and raise the status of their improv from simple games and scenes to high performance art.

The principles of Level 2 separate iO's training center from other improv schools by focusing on bold decision making and group support. Students will work together to commit to each other's choices and elevate those choices, creating truly unique and inspiring moments of improvisation.

Level 2 is an 8-week course that meets once a week for 3 hours. At the end of the term, each class will have a short 10-minute performance demonstration open to the public.
classes.location: 1501 N. Kingsbury St., Chicago, IL 60642

classes.title: iO Improv Level 3: Thursdays from 7-10pm
classes.description:
Level 3 redirects the focus back on to the essential building block of longform improvisation, the two person scene. The exercises in this level will help students slow down and find grounded real points of view and relationships to explore in their scenes. Rather than act like cartoon characters, Level 3 helps students understand that by listening and reacting to what someone is saying to them, they can create compelling and emotional scenes that will naturally evolve into comedy. Students will learn to develop the natural instincts that will help their scenes flourish and connect with audiences and will receive individualized feedback from their instructor about their strengths and opportunities for growth.

'Every line is golden and every detail is golden.' The principles of Level 3 help reassure students that they already have everything they need to create a great scene. Students will stop "inventing" and start truly improvising with guidance on how to respond with real emotions and committed character choices.

Level 3 is an 8-week course that meets once a week for 3 hours. At the end of the term, each class will have a short 10-minute performance demonstration open to the public.
classes.location: 1501 N. Kingsbury St., Chicago, IL 60642

classes.title: iO Improv Level 4: Thursdays from 7-10pm
classes.description:
Level 4 synthesizes the lessons from all of the previous levels and allows students to begin creating longform pieces that are cohesive, thoughtful, and artistic. Students will learn a variety of classic longform pieces in an effort to understand how structure can inform their art. Each form taught will offer students an opportunity to learn how a form can be a motivator of creativity and authenticity, and not just a rigid structure to adhere to. The skills in this class will help students perform longer sets and will encourage true improvisational exploration of ideas, concepts, and thoughts–urging students to actually say something with their art.

Learn the rules, obey the rules, then break the rules. Additional focus will be given to iO's signature longform style, The Harold. Developed and performed at iO for the last 35 years, the Harold is now taught and performed all over the world and is a sophisticated and rewarding form that lends itself to all styles of improvisation. Students will learn the intricacies of performing the Harold with the understanding that the form is just a launching point for inspiration and not a destination in and of itself.

Level 4 is an 8-week course that meets once a week for 3 hours. At the end of the term, each class will have a short 10-minute performance demonstration open to the public.
classes.location: 1501 N. Kingsbury St., Chicago, IL 60642

classes.title: iO Improv Level 5: Thursdays from 7-10pm
classes.description:
This level is the culminating class of the iO program and is followed by an 8-week run of performances on Sunday nights from January 10th, 2027 through February 28th, 2027, for which you do not pay tuition.

Level 5 pushes students into a true ensemble mindset and challenges the groups to create their own unique longform piece. Inspired by their work in Level 4 and all the previous levels, students will work together under the guidance and assistance of their instructor to brainstorm and generate a new, unique form that will be performed on stage. This level allows for a lot of personalized notes and diagnostics from the instructor and really helps students grow as individuals while also operating in an ensemble state of mind.

At the end of this 8 week course, the students will spend the following 8 weeks performing their devised piece on stage at iO every Sunday night. Following the completion of level 5 and their performances, all iO graduates will be eligible to audition for the House Team program at iO, allowing them to continue their education and perform on a coached ensemble with weekly rehearsals and semi-weekly shows, sponsored by the theater.
classes.location: 1501 N. Kingsbury St., Chicago, IL 60642

classes.title: Storytelling Level One
classes.description:
Want to learn how to tell a story and connect to people from one of the best storytellers in NYC? Magnet Theater Storytelling Instructor Adam Wade (20-time Moth Story Slam Champion, Creator of the Best Selling Audible Original, You Ought To Know Adam Wade) will teach you how to take personal experiences from your life and create stories that are universal and identifiable for an audience. You'll be blown away at how engaging and relatable your personal stories can be! Whether you're a Moth Slam Champion in the making, a writer seeking to fine-tune your narrative skills, or someone who wants the confidence and ability to get in front of people and be heard -- this class will help.

In this class, you will learn the basic elements of telling a narrative story, how to take a crowd by surprise and make them care, how to be real and truthful on stage, and how to discover and communicate the real meaning behind your experience. Classes will include verbal and written exercises and various techniques and approaches to prepare yourself for a performance of your story.

Just some of the things that you'll get out of the class: a higher level of self-confidence, at least one polished, five-to-six-minute story -- which could be a Moth Story Slam winner, the beginning of a one-person show or personal essay, and the fundamentals needed to develop future stories.

The class concludes with a graduation performance where you will perform your personal story in front of a live, super-supportive audience!

Since 2010, Adam has helped over 3,500 students with their own stories in these Storytelling Classes at Magnet Theater.

classes.title: Solo Character Weekend Intensive: January 9th & 10th
classes.description:
This weekend-long intensive will give you the tools to generate, develop, and deepen your solo characters. Sharpen your character writing and performing skills and learn to draw from many sources of inspiration to create solo characters that are hilarious, memorable, lovable, hate-able, charming, and strange. Explore various styles of solo characters, how to set your characters up for success, and how to use improvisation to expand your characters into a fully fleshed out solo pieces!

Our weekend long intensive will meet January 9th - 10th from 11am-5pm, with an hour break for lunch each day from 1:30-2:30pm.

Come learn at the best improv theater in the world all while making new friends in one of the best cities in the world!

Interested? Want more information? Please e-mail classes@ioimprov.com for all questions.

classes.description: This class is exclusively for students who are both writers and actors. Students will pitch ideas, write and rewrite, produce, and act in their own sketches. The end result is a class show written and performed entirely by the students. In this class, students will learn the mechanics of putting together a sketch show where they are responsible for all the show's aspects (even some sketch directing elements).

classes.title: Writing for Animated Television
classes.description:
From edgy adult series like “Rick & Morty” and “Primal” to groundbreaking family shows like “Bluey” and “Infinity Train,” animation on television is a varied and exciting landscape full of storytelling possibility!

In this class students will develop their idea for an animated television series, taking it from initial concept to fully fleshed out pitch document.

Along the way students will learn the fundamentals of how these shows are created and how writing for them may differ from traditional live-action.

We’ll cover crafting a strong core concept, creating fully realized animated characters, building out the world of your show, writing clear loglines, and pitching with confidence.

classes.title: Writing 1
classes.description:
Writing 1 is for any student who is looking to start the journey of writing to and for a Second City-style revue. This class is the foundation for scenic comedy writing, a guide for utilizing an improviser’s skill set for rapid creation, and learning writing refinement. The concepts and tools provided in Writing 1 are the building blocks for being able to quickly and creatively write to and for a Second City-style revue. Every comedic writer must have the knowledge and skills that are offered in this course.

Writing 1 teaches students how to write comedic scenes that could be found in a Second City-style revue by exploring different scenic set-ups, character dialogue, genres and point-of-view. Students use improv as a tool for character and dialogue generation.

Writing 1 class time includes a combination of solo exercises and collaborative exercises to build skills in brainstorming, comedic structure and character development. Students also gain a Second City perspective on theatrical writing – including observation, idea generation, dialogue, and character creation. Feedback focuses on ‘what works’ in terms of the structural building blocks. Class time is active, positive and encouraging. Students practice concepts through a series of weekly homework assignments.

Any student interested in creating Second City-style comedic writing or interested in extending their improvisation abilities and experiences into writing should take Writing 1.

classes.description:
Improv for Anxiety (IFAX) – Beginner

A 7-week introduction to the art of improvisation and the tools it offers to help us deal with social anxiety.

This innovative class uses ensemble-based improv to help people manage feelings of stress and anxiety. A Second City instructor will lead the class through a series of improv exercises that are specifically chosen to help students focus on the present, step outside of their comfort zones, and embrace the unknown in a welcoming and low-pressure environment.

About The Second City’s Improv for Anxiety Program

The Improv for Anxiety Program aims to build a nurturing space and student community where students can slowly explore the tenets of improvisation while receiving accommodations due to feelings of fear or anxiety.

The Improv for Anxiety Program is not a substitute for therapy. Instructors focus on teaching improvisational skills such as listening, being others focused, taking risks, and working from a “Yes, And…” mindset.

It gives you a strong foundation for TV and film writing, demystifies the language and process of writing, and gives you the tools to begin turning your great idea into the next Citizen Kane/Troop Beverly Hills (same thing).

You’ll learn about the language of film/TV writing, the importance of deadlines, the unique qualities of a cinematic story versus a sketch, lots of screenplay formatting, how and what to pitch, and the scale of your ideas.

You’ll watch films and TV shows with a critical ear for dialogue and structure, read scripts, learn how to pitch, pitch those great ideas, and create outlines or treatments for that million-dollar sitcom or film idea. Oh, and table reads!

This course is a great introduction to the Comedy TV Pilots and Writing for Late Night programs.

While 'Yes, And' is the guiding ethos in improvisation, students will go above and beyond that simple principle and learn how acceptance, agreement, honesty, connections, listening, and commitment will help them discover the truth in comedy. classes.title: Just Roll With It! Improv for Dungeons & Dragons
classes.description:
Whether you’re a novice adventurer or an experienced Dungeon Master looking to sharpen your skills, this course will help you bring more confidence, creativity, and fun to your D&D campaigns.

Over five weeks, we’ll explore improv techniques through roleplay, character work, collaborative storytelling, D&D-focused exercises, and plenty of dice rolling to help you become a stronger roleplayer, storyteller, and Dungeon Master. You’ll create memorable characters, make bold choices, react in the moment, build stronger party chemistry, tell better stories together, and learn to confidently roll with whatever the game throws at you.

The course culminates in a live Dungeons & Dragons adventure where students bring their characters to life and put everything they’ve learned into practice. Live on the WGIS Theater Stage, open for friends and family to watch!

Watch past student show here: https://youtu.be/4R50R92b3aI

It’s also a great place to meet other D&D players, make new friends, and connect with like-minded people. You might even find your next campaign along the way.

For players, we’ll explore how to stay true to your character while making choices that move the game forward, use your stats and backstory to inspire roleplay, build meaningful relationships with other characters, and create characters that feel like real people instead of just a collection of abilities.

You’ll also create multiple characters that you’ll develop and bring to life throughout the course, exploring their wants, beliefs, flaws, relationships, backstory, and point of view as you put them into new situations each week.

For those interested in Dungeon Mastering, we’ll cover practical tools for creating memorable NPCs, compelling villains and mysteries, character-specific story hooks, cinematic descriptions and combat, preserving player autonomy, and adapting when your players inevitably do something you never planned for.

And if you’re a player only this section is still for you! You’ll get a peek behind the DM screen and learn how players can make their DM’s job easier through dynamic backstories, character hooks, bold choices, and collaborative storytelling. Great D&D isn’t the DM telling the players a story. It’s a story everyone at the table creates together.

Topics include:

• Creating memorable characters with wants, beliefs, bonds & flaws
• Thinking on your feet while staying true to your character
• Yes, And, commitment, curious listening & making bold choices
• Character voices, emotions, stats & points of view
• Party chemistry & collaborative storytelling
• NPCs, villains, mysteries & character-specific story hooks
• DM descriptions, world-building & cinematic combat
• Adapting when the players, story, or dice change your plans

Whether you’re still getting comfortable at the table, have years of adventures under your belt, or want to become a more confident DM, this class will help you get more out of your next campaign.

classes.title: AP1 - Sundays with TBD T127
classes.description:
AP1: Chicago Improv for Beginners

AP1 is an all-encompassing survey course that will give anyone a solid foundation in improvisational comedy – whether you want to perform, direct, write, or just know more.

New to improv? This class is for you. AP1 introduces you to Chicago's approach to improv by covering a wide variety of concepts:​

• The rules of Improv and breaking the rules
• Group mind (the myth, the facts)
• How to say "yes, and" and when to say “no”
• Finding or Creating the game
• Long-form
• Short-form
• Writing via improv
• Direction (taking and giving)
• Object and environment work
• Introducing a show

This class will culminate in an optional student showcase at The Annoyance on the final Sunday of the term.

Prerequisite: None
classes.location: 851 W Belmont Ave, Chicago, IL

classes.title: AP2 - Sundays with TBD T127
classes.description:
AP2: Beginning Annoyance Philosophy - Initiations

AP2 is an immersive examination of The Annoyance philosophy on, and approach to, improv. AP2 focuses on decisive initiations and a strong point of view. This class focuses on the first seconds of scenes and explores how they affect the rest of the scene.

In AP2, you will cover:

• Personal responsibility in a scene − taking care of yourself and your choices
• Trusting instincts
• Creating/Finding “Your Deal” at the top of the scene
• Beginning character development
• Object work as inspiration
• Environment as inspiration
• The responsibility of operating without censorship.
• Individual feedback and tendencies

This class will culminate in an optional student showcase at The Annoyance on the final Sunday of the term.

Prerequisite:
AP1 or sufficient background in improv. Please let us know in the comments section below where you have studied so that we may contact them to confirm.
classes.location: 851 W Belmont Ave, Chicago, IL

classes.title: AP3 - Sundays withTBD T127
classes.description:
AP3: Scene Work

AP3 is about taking that next step in scenes. While AP2 focused on the beginning moments of a scene, in AP3 students are challenged to play with more complexity and style, juggling it all within a scene while always maintaining their strong point of view.

Aspects of this class include:

• Acknowledging the realities of your scene partner
• Scenic development: Finding the Highways and Bi-ways of a scene to extend its length
• Managing context without getting in your head (the who/what/where/when/why/etc.)
• Creating specific, surprising choices
• Playing with Opposites and Curve Balls
• Creating and playing with multiple patterns or games in a scene
• In-depth three person and group scene work
• Protecting and Playing the Freak
• Learning how to repair a scene that isn’t working
• Managing forms and style
• DaDa scenes (playing fiercely without needing to “make sense”)
• Justification: how to use it not out of fear but as a tool.
• Personal challenge and goals based on individual feedback

Prerequisite:
Students must have completed AP2 to take this course.
classes.location: 851 W Belmont Ave, Chicago, IL

classes.title: AP4 - Sundays with TBD T127
classes.description:
AP4

Through individual feedback, setting performance goals, and identifying and breaking habits, AP4 offers fine-tuning and involves the following aspects:

• Stretching the performer
• Pushing unique specificity
• Keeping voice in multiple person scenes, split-scenes
• Making rich, varied environments
• Embodying the character and embellishing the world
• Organic improv ∼ developing a scene based on physical and emotional choices

Prerequisite:
Students must have completed AP3 to take this class.
classes.location: 851 W Belmont Ave, Chicago, IL

classes.title: CRASS1 - Sundays with TBD T127
classes.description:
CRASS1: Improv to Sketch

CRASS (CReating Annoyance Style Shows) is a the next step in The Annoyance's process; using improv to create written material.

In CRASS 1, students will take all of the improv skills they've honed in AP1-5 and together with their director, create a written sketch revue. Students will be assigned additional roles outside of actor/writer and may be responsible for costumes, props, etc. These classes are more intensive than AP1-5 and will require additional work and rehearsal outside of class hours.

For over 30 years the Annoyance has specialized in using improv comedy to create full length plays and musicals. From Annoyance classics like Splatter Theater and Co-ed Prison Sluts, to more modern shows like Steamworks: The Musical and Live Laugh Blood, The Annoyance has enjoyed pushing the envelope of what plays and musicals can be.

With this class, students will start the journey of turning their improv into written works, refining, planning, and creating a full sketch revue.

• Using Annoyance style improvisation to build a sketch
• Theatre Roles
• Technical aspects of the theatre

Prerequisite:

Students must have completed AP5 to enroll in this class

Tech:
Tech rehearsal for the shows is 3/14 12-3pm

Shows:
This show will culminate in two (2) showcases - Sundays 3/14, 3/21 6pm

Does writing a script feel intimidating? Does the thought of thirty to ninety pages feel insurmountable, even when you know you have the ideas? Does screenplay format feel like it doesn't suit you? Learn an unconventional and liberating writing process that combines narrative storytelling for TV and film with improvisational dialogue.

This class will introduce you to the creative process behind shows like Curb Your Enthusiasm or films like Best in Show. You'll learn how to shape hyper-distilled pitches into full story outlines built for improvised dialogue. In this course, you will come away with new techniques that strip away many barriers encountered when piecing scripts together and introduce a new set of techniques for comedic storytelling. Using tools like character POV, world building, and practical methods for generating large amounts of material, you will come away from this class with short outlines ready-made for production. The class will culminate in improvised readings of student-written outlines. This style of writing can be a springboard to a conventional script or a totally new way of working. Fuck it, love your ideas, and have fun telling stories!

classes.title: Summer Intensive Part 1 May 10-14
classes.description:
Annoyance 2027 Summer Intensives

5 day course - 6 hours per day with additional 2 hour workshops

PART 1:
The Annoyance Training Center teaches students how to develop and maintain a strong individual voice in their improvisation. These intensives will address the initiation of a scene; developing and maintaining strong characters; learning to hold on to your initial choices while at the same time, expanding on (heightening) the choices you have made; and learning to become deft at creating and weaving unexpected, character-based choices into your work. Annoyance classes challenge the conventional wisdom of the rules of improvisation, examining what’s behind them and how they came to be in the first place. Simply put, we make you the best improviser YOU can be. All of our intensive teachers are ensemble members who have learned and performed with The Annoyance, and thus have first hand experience with the way we approach improvisation.

PART 2:
Took the Intensive Part 1 and want more? Want to go further with your exploration of our philosophy? This is for you! With this intensive sequel, we go deeper into the teachings of The Annoyance, tackling things like context, group scene work, ensemble and much more.

If you can only take one week, take part 1. In The Annoyance Summer intensives, we try to cover all of the information in The Annoyance's AP1-5 program each day - AP1 on Monday, AP2 on Tuesday, and so on. These classes meet for 20 hours over 8 weeks. In these intensives, we're trying to cram that info into 6 hours over one day. A truly impossible task. So, part 2 was created as a way to convey more of the information we couldn't get to in part 1, while also allowing instructors to get deeper into concepts they're passionate about, knowing the students all have at least part 1 under their belt.

PREREQUISITE FOR PART 2:
Students must have previously completed an Annoyance Part 1 Intensive or have completed AP5 within The Annoyance Training Center

SCHEDULE:
Classes: Mon - Fri 10am-5pm with a 1 hour break for lunch (1-2pm)
Optional Workshops: Mon - Thu 5-7pm
Optional Showcase: Fri 6pm

PART 1 WORKSHOPS:
Advanced Improv with Mick Napier
Game-Based Improv with Face Off Unlimited (FOU)

Musical Improv with Tuesday Musical Improv (TMI)
Genre-Based Improv with Hitch*Cocktails

classes.title: SUMMER INTENSIVE 2027
classes.description:
The iO Summer Intensive Program meets every Monday through Thursday from 11am to 5pm for five weeks from July 5th through August 5th 2027.

EARLY BIRD PRICING:
Full Program for $1,700 through March 31st, 2027
Price Increases to $1,800 on April 1st, 2027

Unlike anything you'll ever experience! Spend 5 weeks at the historic iO Theater in Chicago, the birthplace of improvisation, learning long form in its greatest incubator from the world's greatest comedy teachers.

The iO Summer Intensive condenses five levels of our curriculum into five weeks. The class meets every Monday through Thursday from 11am to 5pm for five weeks. Each week, you'll work with a different iO teaching artist on a particular level of curriculum. Best of all, the class culminates in a performance here in our theater!

Week 1 is Level 1 – Ensemble – Introduces the basics of agreement, making strong choices, supporting your partner, exploring pattern, heightening, and intro to long-form.

Week 2 is Level 2 – The Performer’s Skill Set – Focuses on advanced character work and exploring environment, using exercises and games designed to take the improviser out of their head and into the character and the world onstage. Object work, physical investment in character choices, wants & objectives, and advanced listening exercises

Week 3 is Level 3 – Scene Work – Extensive work in two-person improvised scenes sharpens listening skills, emotional choices, and investment in the dynamics of a scene, such as status and “game”. Introduction to editing techniques, tag-outs, walk-ons, and further work with iO’s signature form, The Harold.

Week 4 is Level 4 – Long-form – Incorporating skills learned throughout the previous levels, focus is on building character, relationship, and form with emphasis on grounded scene work as the foundation for long-forms.

Week 5 is Level 5 – Form Creation – Applies the skills from Levels 1-4 to create your own piece. The class focuses on the structure, including openings, group games, and scenes. Advanced pattern work, group work, editing, and scene work are used to explore the challenges and magic of long-form. Students have class shows in addition to weekly class sessions.

Come learn at the best improv theater in the world all while making new friends in one of the best cities in the world!

All Summer Intensive Students will receive an iO Student ID which gets you access to all regular shows for free! It also gets you discount tickets at some other improv theaters in the city.

Interested? Want more information?

Please e-mail classes@ioimprov.com for all questions.

classes.title: Advanced Mapping
classes.description: Mapping scenes are where we treat one thing like it's another. It's an intervention, but about telling someone they need to stop taking selfies. Right? Let's go deep on this. We will use "as if" to expand what we can say yes to, what we relate to. This is slightly heady class, but also a fun one. This will work acting muscles, and you'll have to think about "why" your characters are doing things. But also the scenes are gonna be really fun!
classes.location: WGIS Studio 2, 1613 N. Vermont Ave., Los Angeles, CA 90027

classes.title: Advanced Refresher
classes.schedule: Tuesdays 11am-2pm PT · Oct 6 - Nov 10 · 6 classes, 1 show
classes.description:
Do scenes, get notes from the amazing improviser / funny person / nice man Eugene Cordero. Eugene has been a top improviser for literal decades, playing with such amazing teams such as The Smokes and Reuben Williams. He's taught and coached at UCB for years and years. In recent years, he's acted in such incredible shows such as Loki, Tacoma FD, and the Mandalorian. But he loves improv too much and has come back to help you get a good refresher on some solid scenework.

This is for ADVANCED IMPROVISERS only. You must have taken four multi-week courses at any long form theater. Like 101-401 at UCB. Or Level 1-3 and Game Drill at WGIS. You must be comfortable with the vocabulary of "game of the scene."

If you're not sure if you qualify, email classes@wgimprovschool.com.

classes.title: Bad Scenes (3 sessions, in-person)
classes.description: Don't ask questions. Don't do transaction scenes. Label the Who, What, Where. Don't talk about someone who isn't there. It's a lot of rules! Of course, they're not rules at all, so let's break them and do all the "bad scenes," but good!

classes.title: Coaching Musical Improv
classes.description:
Coaching a musical team comes with a unique set of challenges: How do you balance improv scenework and songs? How do you vary up practice sessions to keep things interesting? How do you prepare groups for successful shows? In this four-week course, students will get hands on experience running exercises and giving notes to up-and-coming musical improvisers. They will also receive personalized feedback from the head of Musical Improv Program to help them meet those challenges and be the best coach they can be! Pre-requisite: Magnet Musical 3

classes.title: Craig Cackowski's Improv Class
classes.description: This is an ongoing workshop that addresses fundamental and advanced improv skills. The focus will be on staying grounded, making interesting choices and saying yes, with a little game of the scene mixed in. Students pay for the month. We're hoping to accumulate a core group of regulars who end up doing this months in a row. Next month's classes will be posted at the beginning of the month, and we'll email recent students to let them know first.
classes.location: WGIS Space, 1615 N. Vermont Ave., Los Angeles, CA 90027

classes.title: Create a New Form
classes.schedule: Tuesdays 7pm-10pm PT · Oct 13 - Nov 17 · 6 classes, 1 show
classes.description: Harold is king but that doesn't mean there isn't room for exploration! A group of people working together to build something from nothing is the foundation of all great improv groups, no matter the format. In this 6-week workshop participants will be led through a series of exercises highlighting individual skills to build group mind, culminating in an original longform piece. The exercises used in this workshop can also be helpful in creating a new format for your indie group or to push your Harold work further by experimenting beyond the three beat structure. The new form developed in class will debut for the first time in a show on the stage!
classes.location: WGIS Studio 2, 1613 N. Vermont Ave., Los Angeles, CA 90027

classes.title: Empathy Driven Improv
classes.description:
Having trouble making choices? Make your scenes easier by slowing down your scene work and tapping into what you would do in real life. Think less about "getting it right" by using your gut response to inform your improv response. Keep heightened scenes simple by using your own experiences as a touchstone for choices, staying committed and using the environment.

Note: Class will end between 2:30pm and 3pm pending on that week's exercises.

Please note: There will be no class on 10/18

classes.description: Doing a great ten minute scene is very different than doing a great one minute scene. This class will be focused on solid, grounded, two person scenes. We'll hone our listening and commitment skills and learn how to plumb the depths of our characters to get meaty, satisfying, hilarious scenes that last longer than a few minutes. This will be a rust-busting scenework heavy class focused on building our basic scenework chops and dropping our sense of panic in two person scene work. Prerequisite: Magnet Level 3 or Instructor approval.

classes.title: Storytelling Level One
classes.description:
Want to learn how to tell a story and connect to people from one of the best storytellers in NYC? Magnet Theater Storytelling Instructor Adam Wade (20-time Moth Story Slam Champion, Creator of the Best Selling Audible Original, You Ought To Know Adam Wade) will teach you how to take personal experiences from your life and create stories that are universal and identifiable for an audience. You'll be blown away at how engaging and relatable your personal stories can be! Whether you're a Moth Slam Champion in the making, a writer seeking to fine-tune your narrative skills, or someone who wants the confidence and ability to get in front of people and be heard -- this class will help.

In this class, you will learn the basic elements of telling a narrative story, how to take a crowd by surprise and make them care, how to be real and truthful on stage, and how to discover and communicate the real meaning behind your experience. Classes will include verbal and written exercises and various techniques and approaches to prepare yourself for a performance of your story.

Just some of the things that you'll get out of the class: a higher level of self-confidence, at least one polished, five-to-six-minute story -- which could be a Moth Story Slam winner, the beginning of a one-person show or personal essay, and the fundamentals needed to develop future stories.

The class concludes with a graduation performance where you will perform your personal story in front of a live, super-supportive audience!

Since 2010, Adam has helped over 3,500 students with their own stories in these Storytelling Classes at Magnet Theater.
classes.location: Cre8ive NYC, 134 West 29th Street. 2nd Floor, New York
